issues.problem: Line 11 is the bug: it makes a singleton capture the transient typed client and its handler. The scenario only reproduces because lines 7-10 set an explicit HttpClientHandler, which means an infinite PooledConnectionLifetime. With the .NET 9+ default handler the connections would recycle with HandlerLifetime. A candidate could argue that line 7 is also a cause. The explanation says lines 7-10 are not a defect by themselves, which is defensible, but the answer text does not state the condition.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally add one sentence to the answer in both locales: the explicit HttpClientHandler (infinite PooledConnectionLifetime) is what makes the pinned handler hold on to the old connections, and the singleton registration on line 11 is the defect to fix.
